reviews.text: They are good but they're hours of operations is inconsistent. I tried to bring  my dog in at 545pm, 15mins before  closing. The clinic was closed then I tried calling them but no answer. Very frustrating when you're trying to get care for your fur baby.
Excellent place for our pets, good treatment and good medical service.

I was referred by several people and I'm so glad we took Kitty today. He was diagnosed with a UTI. Everyone was kind and helpful. Gilley's is not only knowledgeable, reputable, professional,  and kind but additionally... affordable! Thanks for helping Kitty.

My precious cat, Kitty, has a UTI. This was our 1st visit at Gilley's. The entire staff was so kind, polite, and professional. They diagnosed and cared for Kitty. We left there with everything we needed for ongoing care. But, most importantly... it was affordable! I'm a disabled Senior on a fixed income. Kitty is my emotional support animal of OVER 9 years and he's VERY important to me. I was scared of this unexpected,  unknown,  emergency expense. It was such a relief when I saw our bill. So, professional,  reliable,  knowledgeable,  reputable (we received several references for them) AND... affordable.  Thank you to all the staff. I was quite overwhelmed this morning. Thanks from Patty and Reese

This clinic takes walk-ins, and we were so grateful for that! Despite not having an appointment the staff took great care of our Belgian Malinois 7 week old puppy. We were nervous because we came to pick up our puppy in the area but wanted her to have a check up before we drove back to Tampa Bay. We were grateful that Gillet Animal clinic was able to see her as a walk-in patient. Thank you to the Gilley Animal Clinic team!
There is no better pla e to take my dog. They are old school. No computer but paper and files. The price is amazing. The vet is amazong.

I want to sincerely thank the entire team at this veterinary clinic for the exceptional care they gave my dog today.

From the moment we arrived, everyone treated him with kindness, compassion, and professionalism. They monitored him throughout the entire day, kept a close eye on him, and made me feel confident that he was in the best hands.

What impressed me the most was their honesty and genuine concern for my dog’s well-being. At no point did I feel pressured into unnecessary treatments. Instead, they took the time to evaluate him carefully and made decisions based on what was truly best for him.

As a pet owner, it’s incredibly comforting to find a veterinary team that truly cares about both the animals and their families. Thank you for your dedication, patience, and the love you showed my dog. I am deeply grateful and highly recommend this clinic to anyone looking for compassionate and trustworthy veterinary care

For 28 years Dr. Gilley and his staff took excellent care of all our animals. He was very compassionate and made sure everything possible was done for our babies. Over the years I recommend Dr Gilley and staff to so many friends. Of course, they were very satisfied. We moved and I cannot stop comparing the vet's here to Dr. Gilley. Again best vet and staff I have ever trusted our animals with. Missing you all. Candy
They are affordable and they take good care of your Dog or Cat.

On April 2, 2026, our son brought our dog Hero to Gillies Animal Clinic in Homestead, Florida, for a county‑mandated rabies vaccine. Hero, an American Bully, was visibly distressed in the lobby—overheating, vomiting, and struggling to breathe. We were told his heart rate was too high and that his temperature was 104, so they advised us to take him home to calm down and return later.
We rushed Hero to the animal clinic on Quail Roos when his condition worsened, and the doctors there tried to save him. They were shocked that Gillies had let him leave in that state. According to them, Hero could have been given anti‑inflammatories or allowed to cool down at the clinic, potentially preventing his death. When we informed Gillies of Hero’s passing, they put us on hold and changed their story, claiming he left in stable condition.
We are devastated and seeking answers. If you were at Gillies Animal Clinic on April 2 and witnessed anything, please reach out. We want to ensure no other family has to go through this.” We will miss our sweet baby Hero.
They are lovely people, they speak English but they are very helpful to Spanish speakers. I would recommend it 100%.

Dr. Gilley saved my dog from having an unnecessary surgery. 100% reliable, honest, and experienced. He has the best prices in town. I really cannot recommend him enough.

WARNING: Do Not Take Your Pet to Gilley Animal Clinic

I’m sharing this in hopes of preventing others from going through what we did. Gilley Animal Clinic almost killed my kitten due to their negligence and misdiagnosis. We brought him in after he was vomiting and not eating. They charged us $320 just to tell us it was “a stomach ache” and sent us home with medication that did nothing.

When our kitten still wasn’t eating and continued to decline, we brought him back the next day. They did another X-ray and finally said there “might” be something in his stomach and recommended we take him to an emergency clinic.

By the time we got him to the emergency vet, he was dangerously dehydrated and already had signs of kidney damage from prolonged vomiting and lack of fluids. He was hospitalized and put on IV fluids for 24 hours just to stabilize him. Still unwell, we took him to a second emergency clinic in Fort Lauderdale, where they did an ultrasound (something Gilley never offered)and immediately found a foreign object in his stomach.
If they would’ve told us that they couldn’t do anything from the start , or done the appropriate diagnostics like an ultrasound, our kitten could have been spared days of pain and life-threatening complications. Instead, we wasted critical time and money, and our pet suffered for it. Rest in peace to our 3 month kitten Judas ❤️
Love all the staff. They really care about the animals 💙
For me, the wait is immense, both for service and even for payment. I went there to deworm my two-month-old puppy, and I think that place is expensive.

We took our 5 week old kitten here and were told he has a minor respiratory infection only to walk in 2 days later and be told there is no such thing a minor respiratory infection, we call again after we leave and they tell us the doctor said he had a SEVERE infection once again at the start when he could be saved they said MINOR INFECTION. They gave us human amoxicillin for this 5 weeks old kitten all they did was slap a "for vetinary use only" sticker on top of it. They keep telling us this was because Coco was a stray, that tellls me enough that they cannot at all do their job.

There is no doubts in my mind Coco could have at least survived longer if we went somewhere else, but instead Coco is dead not even a day after bringing him here. I want the vets to know he died screaming in pain trying his best to survive for us, Before we went here he showed no signs of anything that could go wrong.  Listen to the bad reviews the good ones probably only vaccines.

If your animal has a permanent disease DO NOT go here. They do not ok meds, they don’t call you to tell you you were denied, and make you use amazon or chewy who make you sign for the meds!!! People work. So you go back and forth with Fed Ex. Maybe in 3 weeks you will finally receive your meds. After visiting the dr, calls, emails, texts and more emails and calls. Please streamline your services.

In 1994 I was in search of a sweet pitbull, and my friend Lisa from homestead told me that Dr Gilley had a post in the paper with dogs looking for a home. I called and was told she was brown and sweet, and you were calling her Lady. She came in with a bad case of ringworm, but started pushing her uterus out. The owner never called back, and after the 3rd or 4th time you had no choice but to spay her, and when the owner found out they told you to keep her. I came in to see her and when the girl brought her out I knelt down on one knee and she walked up to me and put her head on my knee and looked up at me with her beautiful eyes. I knew at that moment I had to have her. I want dr Gilley to know it was one of the best decisions I've ever made. I want you to know less than a month later she saved my life...I had run out of gas 100 yards from the gas station at 2 am. I rolled the windows up most of the way, grabbed my gas can and started walking. I was maybe a third of the way there and I got jumped by 2 guys and hit with a bat or pipe. As I layed there one of them said "nice sneakers white boy ( I had recently bought a pair of sweet air jordans) and he also said I better have a stack of cash on me or I'm not making it home tonight. As they both stood over me with the one guy holding the pipe/bat up in the air about to hit me...Pebbles (her new name) came out of nowhere and launched herself onto the guy with the weapon and grabbed the guys arm with her teeth and did a crocodile type death roll with him. He let go of the weapon and backed off. She stood over me literally and barked, growled, and stood her ground till they left. About then I started realizing what had just happened, but didn't understand how she got there since the side windows were mostly up. When I got back to my truck I realized the drivers side window was smashed. She dove threw the glass window to save my life, she had a gash on top of her head. I sat there with her balling my eyes out like I am now. I made it my life to give her the best life I possibly could. A few months later I came home to Boston like my parents wanted me too ( like had had enough of hurricane Andrew devistation) my parent told me I couldn't bring Pebbles home, I told them what happened said there's 0% chance of me coming home without her. The agreed and I had her for almost 13 years before I had to put her down and cremated. I will eventuyally be creamated and want our ashes spread together so im with herforever.I really wanna say thank you from the bottom of my heart for her. Smartest dog ever. And I made sure she slept next to me for her entire life...a small dog bed wasn't good enough for her and I had her tattooed on my arm. She will be with me FOREVER

DO NOT TAKE YOUR ANIMAL HERE. I requested bloodwork. They wanted to do xray and bloodwork so I said yes. I paid the $400. I told them I wanted to go back with her and they didn’t let me. After she was in their care, they said she needs to go to ER vet. She was FINE when I brought her in. She’s high energy, runs around everyday, loves playing, eats great for me. They took a long time to bring her out and you don’t get to talk to an actual
DOCTOR- it’s all ‘he said’ ‘she said’ from 3 different assistants. I should have INSISTED I stay with my baby . I thought they were professionals I could
Trust. Within hours of bringing her home she declined FAST after being in their so called care. They killed my dog. DO NOT TRUST THEM.

First let me start off by saying, if I could leave a 10 star review of Gilley Animal Clinic, I would. Dr. Roger Gilley is the most knowledgeable, caring, and honest vet in all of South Florida. He’s highly skilled at his craft and conscientious of everything he does. So much so that my family and I have been taking our pets to his animal clinic for over 20 plus years. Dr. Gilley and his talented team of techs have been there throughout the years to help our young animals grow up strong and healthy, as well as, help them cross over in old age when it’s their time to leave us. Today he performed surgery on my 9-year old dog Lily to remove an aural hematoma, and she’s recovering well here by my side. While there, he displayed a very generous and compassionate act of kindness to us, one of which we are very thankful for and will never forget. It’s very apparent that this is more than just a job to him, but rather Mr. Roger Gilley’s life work, and the legacy he’s creating is one my family and I will always have respect and admiration for. Dr. Gilley and his crew are caring, perceptive, and supportive of not just the needs of the animals but their owners too. We are so grateful to have Gilley’s Animal Clinic in our lives!
